general_background.title: A phosphine can carry a chalcogen feed
general_background.summary: Trioctylphosphine can solubilize elemental selenium or tellurium as a phosphine chalcogenide for colloidal growth. Delivering the chalcogen in this bonded form changes the chemistry that supplies reactive growth species.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: A reactive sulfur feed
general_background.summary: Bis(trimethylsilyl)sulfide can supply sulfur rapidly to a reactive metal precursor in a nonaqueous colloidal route. The resulting rate of sulfur delivery affects the period over which new nuclei can form.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Colloidal PbS Nanocrystals with Size‐Tunable Near‐Infrared Emission: Observation of Post‐Synthesis Self‐Narrowing of the Particle Size Distribution

general_background.title: Nucleation and size focusing
general_background.summary: A rapid change in precursor availability can create a short nucleation period followed by growth on existing particles. Growth can narrow the size distribution while material is supplied, whereas later ripening can consume smaller particles and change that distribution again.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
